answer.reason: Gaza is the setting of events in the story of Samson and was taken by Judah and foretold to be judged, so a short line can rest on those verses.

clauses.english: was where Samson carried off the city gate doors by night, escaping those lying in wait
clauses.quote: took the doors of the gate of the city, and the two posts

clauses.english: was where the Philistines brought the blinded Samson and bound him in the prison house
clauses.quote: brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass

clauses.english: was taken by Judah with its coast
clauses.quote: Judah took Gaza with the coast thereof

doubts: Jeremiah 47:1 (Pharaoh smote Gaza) and the prophecies of its desolation (Amos 1, Zephaniah 2, Zechariah 9) were left out as prophecy rather than event.

Gaza being taken by Judah (Judges 1:18) is omitted from the line's final form only if the editor wants fewer clauses; the Samson clauses are the chief ones, and these two could be merged by the editor, though two events should not be joined.
